Gallup: Drop in U.S. Catholic Church Attendance Under Pope Francis Sharpest in Decades

Okay, I'm going to go on a small tangent/rant for a moment.

This article claims that weekly mass attendance for Catholics in the U.S. decreased by 6%. It went from 45% attendance to 39% attendance, which is a difference of 6% of the total Catholic population - so, technically, this could be considered accurate.

Now, I'm not really going to criticize this article too much, because they don't seem to be shilling for the Pope with this use of statistics... but the imprecise way that people commonly use statistics can be extremely misleading to anyone giving a cursory glance at their information, or to people who aren't very good at math. That's not just a problem in this article, but from information sources all over.

So what's the problem here? If attendance dropped from 45% to 39% of ALL Catholics, that is just 6% of total Catholics, true. And 6% is significant, but not a lot to many people's minds. But that statistic isn't very meaningful, since a most Catholics don't attend weekly mass to begin with. This is like saying "less than 0.1% of believers in Jesus worldwide have stopped attending Catholic mass in the United States." That's an exaggerated analogy, of course, but it is the same principle.

If weekly attendance dropped from 45% to 39% of all Catholics... that means actual attendance dropped by over 13% - more than double what their article seems to highlight.

If you used to go to a church with 99 other regular attendees, you now are likely to show up with 85 or 86 other people. That's a notably different experience than most people would think of when they read 6%.
